gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the battery in the Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 40L lasted just over 23 hours as a 4 °C fridge in Eco mode in independent tests reported by ESS News, less than half of Anker's 52-hour claim, and about 16 hours as a −18 °C freezer.
standout_why: I compared against these pages: OutdoorGearLab (cited, updated 2025-07-28), GearJunkie (2026-10-31), Outdoor Life (2024-11-22), CarCampSetup and AWDCamper. OutdoorGearLab measured steady-state DC draw for the Dometic CFX5 45 (6.8 W), the BougeRV 23 qt (8.3 W) and the first-generation Anker Everfrost 40 (5.8 W). It does not test the EverFrost 2 or the ICECO VL45. GearJunkie lists the EverFrost 2 40 as 'runs up to 36 hours at 39°F' and does not say whether it measured that. No page has a battery-runtime test of the EverFrost 2 or a measured daily energy figure for the VL45. CarCampSetup and AWDCamper say they did not measure anything. I could not check the second cited page, gearandhome.com (TLS certificate error), or caranddriver.com (fetch blocked), so they may already hold something similar.
decides: ChatGPT offers 'Need a built-in battery' as a path. For that shopper, the ESS News result means planning on about one day per 288 Wh EverFrost 2 battery as a fridge, not the two-plus days Anker advertises. Adding a second battery or a power station becomes part of the decision. For the power-station path, OutdoorGearLab's 6.8 W on the Dometic CFX5 45 and RV Precision's 6.44 Ah per day on the ICECO VL45 back up the efficiency of ChatGPT's premium and rugged picks. Those tests were in a 75 °F lab and a 60–65 °F garage. ChatGPT's '1–2 days on 500 Wh' sounds pessimistic at mild temperatures, but no source here measured in heat.

findings.label: Battery runtime as a fridge, independent test
findings.value: just over 23 h at 4 °C, Eco mode, one 288 Wh battery
findings.source_title: Hands-on with the Anker Solix EverFrost 2 battery-powered cooler (ESS News, Tristan Rayner, 2025-10-02)
findings.note: The article says this came from 'independent testers that ESS News contacted'. It reviews the 40L but does not say outright which size the testers ran, and it gives no ambient temperature. 288 Wh ÷ 23 h ≈ 12.5 W average, assuming all 288 Wh is usable.

findings.label: Battery runtime as a freezer, independent test
findings.value: about 16 h at −18 °C, one 288 Wh battery
findings.source_title: Hands-on with the Anker Solix EverFrost 2 battery-powered cooler (ESS News, Tristan Rayner, 2025-10-02)
findings.note: Same testers and caveats as the fridge result. 288 Wh ÷ 16 h ≈ 18 W average.

findings.label: Maker's runtime claim, for comparison
findings.note: The page has no footnote for the 52 h figure. Its footnote for the two-battery 4.3-day claim gives the test as an empty cooler, Eco mode, 39 °F inside, 77 °F ambient. The US page returned HTTP 429, so this is the global page set to the United States.

findings.label: Steady-state DC power draw, lab
findings.source_title: The Best Electric Coolers | Lab Tested & Ranked (OutdoorGearLab, updated 2025-07-28)
findings.note: Measured on DC with energy meters on identical batteries over 6 h, 75 °F lab, held at 35 °F. It reached 37 °F in about 30 min half-filled with room-temperature cans and hit −2.2 °F minimum. OutdoorGearLab's own estimate is about 320 Wh over 48 h. This rival is cited, so the figure is not new.

findings.label: Steady-state DC power draw, lab
findings.source_title: The Best Electric Coolers | Lab Tested & Ranked (OutdoorGearLab, updated 2025-07-28)
findings.note: Same method as the Dometic test. Dropped below 40 °F in 80 min and took 130–150 min to reach 35 °F. Minimum −3.2 °F. The display read 3.0 °F off the actual temperature. This rival is cited, so the figure is not new.

findings.label: Steady-state DC power draw, lab
findings.source_title: The Best Electric Coolers | Lab Tested & Ranked (OutdoorGearLab, updated 2025-07-28)
findings.note: This is the older model with a 299 Wh battery and should not be read as an EverFrost 2 figure. At 5.8 W the battery would last about 51 h, versus the roughly 23 h ESS News reported for the EverFrost 2. The conditions differ (75 °F lab and 35 °F setpoint vs 4 °C setpoint and unstated ambient).

findings.label: 24 h battery use as a fridge
findings.value: 6.44 Ah in 24 h at 39 °F (100 Ah AGM fell to 93.7%)
findings.source_title: ICECO VL45 Portable Refrigerator/Freezer Review (RVB Precision, Roy Bertalotto, 2019-12-10, updated later)
findings.note: Ambient was about 60–65 °F in a garage. 6.44 Ah × 12 V ≈ 77 Wh per day, about 3.2 W average. This is a 2019 unit, and the current VL45 may differ.

findings.label: 24 h battery use as a freezer, plus pull-down current
findings.value: 100 Ah AGM fell to 89.4% after 24 h in freezer mode; 4.1 A during pull-down; 15 min to 39 °F on MAX
findings.source_title: ICECO VL45 Portable Refrigerator/Freezer Review (RVB Precision, Roy Bertalotto, 2019-12-10, updated later)
findings.note: Same garage as above. 10.6% of 100 Ah ≈ 10.6 Ah ≈ 127 Wh per day at 12 V. AGM state-of-charge readings are approximate.
